component.name: Kurier
component.summary: Start coding agents as subprocesses and drive their sessions

description.p: Kurier is a client for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), the open standard a coding agent speaks over a JSON-RPC connection on stdio. It starts the agent as a subprocess, keeps its session, and shows you what the agent says while it works.

The agent decides which model does the work; kurier owns the environment around it — which directory the session runs in, what the agent is allowed to do, and which MCP servers it may reach. A session record says what is reachable, never what is allowed, so every request is checked again, every time.

ul.li: Start, list, resume and cancel agent sessions, from the command line or from a window
Watch one prompt turn stream in, and stop it without killing the session
Answer the agent's permission requests yourself — kurier denies by default rather than approving for you
One agent needs no driver: opencode today, anything that speaks ACP tomorrow

description.p: The first release with installable packages. Kurier can now log you in to your model providers itself, and the Flatpak brings its own copy of OpenCode.

ul.li: Log in to a model provider from Kurier, with a browser sign-in or an API key, for every provider the agent offers. No terminal needed.
The Flatpak includes OpenCode, which runs with its own settings and login, separate from any OpenCode already on your computer, and has network access to reach its provider.
A clearer message when your account has no credit left, instead of a message that looks like a failed login.
Fixes for Windows and macOS: agents installed as command shims are found, and the agent's working directory is handled correctly.
Packages for Debian and Ubuntu (.deb), Fedora (.rpm), AppImage, macOS, Windows and Flatpak. They are not signed yet.

description.p: The first release of Kurier, a desktop client for the Agent Client Protocol — the open standard a coding agent speaks over. Kurier starts an agent such as OpenCode as a program on your own computer, keeps the conversation, and shows you what the agent says while it works. The agent and the model behind it are not part of Kurier: you install and log in to those yourself.
This first version does the following:

ul.li: A list of your sessions on the left, so you can pick up an earlier conversation instead of starting over.
One real turn with the agent: the answer arrives piece by piece while the agent works, and Stop ends the turn without closing the session.

When the agent asks permission to do something, a dialog asks you, and you can allow it once or refuse it. There is deliberately no "always allow" button: a permission nobody sees again is a permission nobody revoked.
A layout that fits a phone as well as a desktop, down to a window width of 360 pixels.

description.p: Not in this release: several agents side by side, a web version, and a Telegram bot. The command line client is here already. And the Flatpak is an installer rather than a sandbox — an agent has to run on your computer, so Kurier asks for access to your files and to the session bus.
